title: Kadesh and Meribah
lead: Kadesh (Kadesh-barnea), an oasis on the southern edge of Canaan, was Israel's main base in the wilderness. There the scouts returned, Miriam died, and Moses struck the rock at the waters of Meribah, "quarrel" (Numbers 13:26; 20:1–13).

sections.b: Kadesh appears in Abraham's time as En-mishpat (Genesis 14:7) and near Hagar's well (Genesis 16:14). Israel camps there for "many days" (Deuteronomy 1:46), and it marks the southern border of the land (Numbers 34:4; Ezekiel 47:19). It is usually placed at Ein el-Qudeirat in northeastern Sinai. The name Meribah is given both to the rock at Horeb (Exodus 17:7) and to the waters at Kadesh (Numbers 20:13), and the Psalms recall it as a warning (Psalm 81:7; 95:8; 106:32).
